pr.body:
We're adding one more step in the GitHub integration installation pipeline, namely GitHub OAuth2 authorize. This is transparent from the UX perspective as the data exchange happens without user interaction.

The pipeline will now fail in these cases:
- If there is a mismatch between currently authenticated GitHub user (derived from OAuth2 authorize step) and the user who installed the GitHub app (https://github.com/apps/sentry-io)
- If there is a mismatch between `state` parameter supplied by user and pipeline signature
- If GitHub could not generate correct `access_token` from the `code` (wrong or attempt of re-use of `code`).

In all those cases, this error is shown:
![image](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry/assets/1127549/18923861-2ead-4cf5-adda-7738aef801d7)
pr.title: fix(security): validate GitHub user during integration installation

raw_findings.body: The dictionary lookup raises KeyError, producing an unhandled 500 error page instead of the intended rendered installation-failure dialog, and the user cannot complete or diagnose the install.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled exception (HTTP 500) in the installation pipeline instead of a controlled error response.
raw_findings.impact: The dictionary lookup raises KeyError, producing an unhandled 500 error page instead of the intended rendered installation-failure dialog, and the user cannot complete or diagnose the install.
raw_findings.root_cause: New verification code assumes metadata["sender"]["login"] always exists, but build_integration only populates it for webhook-sourced state.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use a safe lookup, e.g. `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")`, and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` when the sender is unknown, mirroring the existing guard in installation.py (`if "sender" not in integration.metadata`).
raw_findings.title: KeyError when integration metadata has no "sender" during install verification
raw_findings.trigger: A GitHub Integration row exists for the installation_id but has no OrganizationIntegration and its metadata lacks the "sender" key (e.g. it was created by the Sentry-initiated pipeline via build_integration, which only sets metadata["sender"] when state.get("sender") is truthy, or by an older install predating sender storage). The user then re-runs the installation flow and reaches this branch.

raw_findings.body: `get_user_info` calls `resp.raise_for_status()`, so an HTTPError propagates out of the pipeline view and the user gets a 500 page instead of the intended "Invalid installation request." dialog; the following `if "login" not in authenticated_user_info` guard never runs for these cases.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unhandled exception escapes the pipeline view, yielding a 500 rather than the designed error page.
raw_findings.impact: `get_user_info` calls `resp.raise_for_status()`, so an HTTPError propagates out of the pipeline view and the user gets a 500 page instead of the intended "Invalid installation request." dialog; the following `if "login" not in authenticated_user_info` guard never runs for these cases.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new code treats get_user_info as returning a dict on failure, but that helper raises on non-2xx responses.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the `get_user_info(...)` call in try/except (requests.RequestException / Exception) and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure, consistent with the token-exchange error handling directly above.
raw_findings.title: Unhandled HTTP error from get_user_info aborts the OAuth pipeline step
raw_findings.trigger: GitHub returns a non-2xx response for GET https://api.github.com/user (token revoked between issuance and use, rate limiting, or a GitHub 5xx) while a user is completing the install flow.

raw_findings.body: The `state` check at `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature` cannot detect a forged/replayed callback, because an attacker can trivially predict the value and drive a victim's browser to /extensions/github/setup/?code=<attacker code>&state=<known constant>, binding the attacker's GitHub login into the victim's pipeline state; the claimed CSRF protection is not actually provided.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Security control is ineffective: state validation always passes for a predictable value.
raw_findings.impact: The `state` check at `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature` cannot detect a forged/replayed callback, because an attacker can trivially predict the value and drive a victim's browser to /extensions/github/setup/?code=<attacker code>&state=<known constant>, binding the attacker's GitHub login into the victim's pipeline state; the claimed CSRF protection is not actually provided.
raw_findings.root_cause: A deterministic, non-secret pipeline identity hash is reused as the OAuth CSRF state token.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Generate a random nonce (e.g. `secrets.token_hex()`), store it with `pipeline.bind_state("oauth_state", nonce)` when redirecting, and compare the callback `state` against that stored per-session nonce instead of `pipeline.signature`.
raw_findings.title: OAuth `state` uses the constant pipeline signature, providing no per-session entropy
raw_findings.trigger: Any installation flow: `Pipeline.signature` is `md5_text(*pipe_ids).hexdigest()` over the pipeline view class names, so it is the same deterministic value for every user and every session (the new test even hardcodes it as "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3").

raw_findings.body: gettext extraction no longer collects these previously-marked strings (they were `_("GitHub installation pending deletion.")` inline before), so they drop out of the translation catalogs and are rendered untranslated for non-English users.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Localization regression: strings silently disappear from .po catalogs.
raw_findings.impact: gettext extraction no longer collects these previously-marked strings (they were `_("GitHub installation pending deletion.")` inline before), so they drop out of the translation catalogs and are rendered untranslated for non-English users.
raw_findings.root_cause: Deduplicating the render logic moved translatable literals out of `_()` call sites into function arguments/defaults.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Mark the literals at their definition sites, e.g. define module-level `ERR_*_SHORT = _("GitHub installation pending deletion.")` constants and pass those lazily translated objects into `error(...)`, removing the runtime `_(error_short)` call.
raw_findings.title: Error strings routed through `_(error_short)` are no longer extractable for translation
raw_findings.trigger: Running `makemessages` after this refactor: the literals "GitHub installation pending deletion.", "Github installed on another Sentry organization." and the default "Invalid installation request." are now plain call arguments/defaults and only reach gettext through a variable.

raw_findings.body: The assertion `b"The GitHub installation could not be found."` was replaced by the generic `b"Invalid installation request."`, so the stubbed 404 from /app/installations/{id} and the IntegrationError message it produces are now completely untested while the test name still claims to cover it; regressions in that error path go undetected.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Coverage silently moves from the 404 handling path to the state-mismatch path, leaving the named behavior unverified.
raw_findings.impact: The assertion `b"The GitHub installation could not be found."` was replaced by the generic `b"Invalid installation request."`, so the stubbed 404 from /app/installations/{id} and the IntegrationError message it produces are now completely untested while the test name still claims to cover it; regressions in that error path go undetected.
raw_findings.root_cause: The test was updated with a non-matching OAuth state, changing which code path it covers without renaming or replacing the lost coverage.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use the matching state value so the pipeline advances to the installation step and restore the `"The GitHub installation could not be found."` assertion; add a separate test named for the state-mismatch case.
raw_findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 404 installation path
raw_findings.trigger: The test now passes state "ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05", which does not equal the pipeline signature ("9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" used by every other test in this file), so `OAuthLoginView` short-circuits at the state check and the flow never reaches `build_integration`/`get_installation_info`.

raw_findings.body: The generated authorize URL is malformed and GitHub receives a truncated or wrong redirect_uri, causing the OAuth step to fail with a redirect_uri mismatch and blocking installation on those deployments.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Malformed outbound OAuth authorize URL on non-trivial url-prefix configurations.
raw_findings.impact: The generated authorize URL is malformed and GitHub receives a truncated or wrong redirect_uri, causing the OAuth step to fail with a redirect_uri mismatch and blocking installation on those deployments.
raw_findings.root_cause: Query parameters are concatenated as raw strings rather than percent-encoded.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Build the query with `urllib.parse.urlencode({"client_id": ..., "state": ..., "redirect_uri": ...})` instead of raw f-string interpolation.
raw_findings.title: Authorize redirect builds query string without URL-encoding parameters
raw_findings.trigger: `redirect_uri` comes from `absolute_uri(...)` which depends on the `system.url-prefix` option; any deployment whose URL prefix contains reserved characters (e.g. a path with `&`, `=`, or non-ASCII) is interpolated raw into the query string.

raw_findings.body: All GitHub integration setup tests that embed the literal "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" fail with an opaque string mismatch that gives no hint the pipeline signature changed, making unrelated refactors expensive to debug.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Brittle assertions that fail opaquely on unrelated pipeline changes.
raw_findings.impact: All GitHub integration setup tests that embed the literal "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" fail with an opaque string mismatch that gives no hint the pipeline signature changed, making unrelated refactors expensive to debug.
raw_findings.root_cause: Tests duplicate a value that is derived from production class names rather than referencing its source.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Compute the expected value in the test from `self.pipeline.signature` (or a helper) instead of hardcoding the MD5 digest in each assertion and query string.
raw_findings.title: Tests hardcode the derived pipeline signature MD5
raw_findings.trigger: Any future rename, reorder, or addition of a pipeline view class in `GitHubIntegrationProvider.get_pipeline_views()` changes `md5_text(*pipe_ids).hexdigest()`.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Wrap the `get_user_info(...)` call in try/except (requests.RequestException / Exception) and return `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure, consistent with the token-exchange error handling directly above.
validated_findings.title: Unhandled HTTP error from get_user_info aborts the OAuth pipeline step
validated_findings.trigger: GitHub returns a non-2xx response for GET https://api.github.com/user (token revoked between issuance and use, rate limiting, or a GitHub 5xx) while a user is completing the install flow.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 434 calls `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])`. Repository context shows `get_user_info` at `provider.py:16` calls `resp.raise_for_status()` which raises HTTPError on non-2xx. The new code has no try/except around this call, so HTTP errors propagate as 500 instead of the intended error page.

validated_findings.body: The `state` check at `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature` cannot detect a forged/replayed callback, because an attacker can trivially predict the value and drive a victim's browser to /extensions/github/setup/?code=<attacker code>&state=<known constant>, binding the attacker's GitHub login into the victim's pipeline state; the claimed CSRF protection is not actually provided.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Security control is ineffective: state validation always passes for a predictable value.
validated_findings.impact: The `state` check at `request.GET.get("state") != pipeline.signature` cannot detect a forged/replayed callback, because an attacker can trivially predict the value and drive a victim's browser to /extensions/github/setup/?code=<attacker code>&state=<known constant>, binding the attacker's GitHub login into the victim's pipeline state; the claimed CSRF protection is not actually provided.
validated_findings.root_cause: A deterministic, non-secret pipeline identity hash is reused as the OAuth CSRF state token.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Generate a random nonce (e.g. `secrets.token_hex()`), store it with `pipeline.bind_state("oauth_state", nonce)` when redirecting, and compare the callback `state` against that stored per-session nonce instead of `pipeline.signature`.
validated_findings.title: OAuth `state` uses the constant pipeline signature, providing no per-session entropy
validated_findings.trigger: Any installation flow: `Pipeline.signature` is `md5_text(*pipe_ids).hexdigest()` over the pipeline view class names, so it is the same deterministic value for every user and every session (the new test even hardcodes it as "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3").
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim that `pipeline.signature` is predictable/constant is speculative. Repository context shows signature is `md5_text(*pipe_ids).hexdigest()` based on pipeline view class names - while deterministic per deployment, an attacker would need to know the exact pipeline configuration. The test hardcodes a value for testing convenience, not because it's publicly known. No concrete evidence the signature is exposed to attackers.

validated_findings.body: gettext extraction no longer collects these previously-marked strings (they were `_("GitHub installation pending deletion.")` inline before), so they drop out of the translation catalogs and are rendered untranslated for non-English users.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Localization regression: strings silently disappear from .po catalogs.
validated_findings.impact: gettext extraction no longer collects these previously-marked strings (they were `_("GitHub installation pending deletion.")` inline before), so they drop out of the translation catalogs and are rendered untranslated for non-English users.
validated_findings.root_cause: Deduplicating the render logic moved translatable literals out of `_()` call sites into function arguments/defaults.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Mark the literals at their definition sites, e.g. define module-level `ERR_*_SHORT = _("GitHub installation pending deletion.")` constants and pass those lazily translated objects into `error(...)`, removing the runtime `_(error_short)` call.
validated_findings.title: Error strings routed through `_(error_short)` are no longer extractable for translation
validated_findings.trigger: Running `makemessages` after this refactor: the literals "GitHub installation pending deletion.", "Github installed on another Sentry organization." and the default "Invalid installation request." are now plain call arguments/defaults and only reach gettext through a variable.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The claim about gettext extraction is speculative. The code at line 141 shows `_(error_short)` where `error_short` is a string parameter with default value. Python gettext tools can extract string literals from default parameter values. No concrete evidence that extraction actually fails.

validated_findings.body: The assertion `b"The GitHub installation could not be found."` was replaced by the generic `b"Invalid installation request."`, so the stubbed 404 from /app/installations/{id} and the IntegrationError message it produces are now completely untested while the test name still claims to cover it; regressions in that error path go undetected.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Coverage silently moves from the 404 handling path to the state-mismatch path, leaving the named behavior unverified.
validated_findings.impact: The assertion `b"The GitHub installation could not be found."` was replaced by the generic `b"Invalid installation request."`, so the stubbed 404 from /app/installations/{id} and the IntegrationError message it produces are now completely untested while the test name still claims to cover it; regressions in that error path go undetected.
validated_findings.root_cause: The test was updated with a non-matching OAuth state, changing which code path it covers without renaming or replacing the lost coverage.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use the matching state value so the pipeline advances to the installation step and restore the `"The GitHub installation could not be found."` assertion; add a separate test named for the state-mismatch case.
validated_findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the 404 installation path
validated_findings.trigger: The test now passes state "ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05", which does not equal the pipeline signature ("9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" used by every other test in this file), so `OAuthLoginView` short-circuits at the state check and the flow never reaches `build_integration`/`get_installation_info`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch shows test_installation_not_found now uses state `ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05` while other tests use `9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3`. Since state must match `pipeline.signature` (line 412), the mismatched state causes early return at line 413, never reaching the 404 installation path. The test name no longer matches what it tests.

validated_findings.body: The generated authorize URL is malformed and GitHub receives a truncated or wrong redirect_uri, causing the OAuth step to fail with a redirect_uri mismatch and blocking installation on those deployments.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Malformed outbound OAuth authorize URL on non-trivial url-prefix configurations.
validated_findings.impact: The generated authorize URL is malformed and GitHub receives a truncated or wrong redirect_uri, causing the OAuth step to fail with a redirect_uri mismatch and blocking installation on those deployments.
validated_findings.root_cause: Query parameters are concatenated as raw strings rather than percent-encoded.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Build the query with `urllib.parse.urlencode({"client_id": ..., "state": ..., "redirect_uri": ...})` instead of raw f-string interpolation.
validated_findings.title: Authorize redirect builds query string without URL-encoding parameters
validated_findings.trigger: `redirect_uri` comes from `absolute_uri(...)` which depends on the `system.url-prefix` option; any deployment whose URL prefix contains reserved characters (e.g. a path with `&`, `=`, or non-ASCII) is interpolated raw into the query string.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: The trigger scenario requires `system.url-prefix` to contain reserved URL characters like `&` or `=`. This is an extremely unlikely configuration - URL prefixes are typically clean URLs like `https://sentry.example.com`. The `absolute_uri` function returns standard URLs. No evidence this is a realistic trigger.

validated_findings.body: All GitHub integration setup tests that embed the literal "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" fail with an opaque string mismatch that gives no hint the pipeline signature changed, making unrelated refactors expensive to debug.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Brittle assertions that fail opaquely on unrelated pipeline changes.
validated_findings.impact: All GitHub integration setup tests that embed the literal "9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3" fail with an opaque string mismatch that gives no hint the pipeline signature changed, making unrelated refactors expensive to debug.
validated_findings.root_cause: Tests duplicate a value that is derived from production class names rather than referencing its source.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Compute the expected value in the test from `self.pipeline.signature` (or a helper) instead of hardcoding the MD5 digest in each assertion and query string.
validated_findings.title: Tests hardcode the derived pipeline signature MD5
validated_findings.trigger: Any future rename, reorder, or addition of a pipeline view class in `GitHubIntegrationProvider.get_pipeline_views()` changes `md5_text(*pipe_ids).hexdigest()`.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a style/maintainability concern about hardcoded test values, not a bug. The tests work correctly with the hardcoded signature. Future breakage from pipeline changes is speculative and would be caught by test failures.

validated_findings.body: Call sites such as `return error(request, self.active_organization)` do not convey that an HTML failure dialog is rendered, and `from sentry.integrations.github.integration import error` would collide with the ubiquitous generic name, hurting readability and inviting accidental shadowing.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Maintainability: ambiguous symbol name in a shared integration module.
validated_findings.impact: Call sites such as `return error(request, self.active_organization)` do not convey that an HTML failure dialog is rendered, and `from sentry.integrations.github.integration import error` would collide with the ubiquitous generic name, hurting readability and inviting accidental shadowing.
validated_findings.root_cause: Extracted duplicate render logic was given a non-descriptive public name.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Rename the helper to something descriptive such as `render_integration_error_response` (and update the four call sites) or make it a private `_render_error`.
validated_findings.title: New module-level helper is named with the overly generic identifier `error`
validated_findings.trigger: Reading or importing this module: `error` is a public module-level symbol in the same file that also uses `Pipeline.error(...)` semantics, and it shadows the common local variable/parameter name `error` used elsewhere in exception handling.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a pure style concern about naming conventions. The function `error` works correctly and the name collision concern is speculative - there's no evidence of actual shadowing issues in the codebase.
